newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberian bonds to eye dlr/mark movements next week.
newsitem.headline: Iberian bonds to eye dlr/mark movements next week.

text.p: Spanish and Portuguese bonds, currently stuck in slow, holiday trade, will closely watch the dollar/mark next week.

"At present there is a close relationship between bonds and the dollar and the market will focus greatly on the currency and on US indicators," said Henrik Lumholdt, Bank of America economist in Madrid.
The absence of key domestic indicators next week and the slow market activity will force participants to focus on the U.S. and on dollar strength.
"Nothing big is expected next week, not only because of the lack of orders but also because of the absence of economic data", said Valentin Fernandez, chief economist at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
"In Spain the only news will be one-year and 18-month bill auctions as well as three-, five-, 10- and 15- year bonds as well as the regular repurchase tender for central bank certificates," he added.
But Bank of America's Lumholdt said "I don't think the bond auctions will have too much impact on prices, including futures, in such an inactive market."

Fernandez, who expects the Bank of Spain to hold the key money rate steady next week, shares this view and believes both Spain and Portugal will be more concerned with the dollar/mark and the likely implications of the currency movements on the Bundesbank's monetary policy.

"I think most people will be more concerned with the dollar/mark and the implications for the Bundesbank. If the rate goes above 1.85 marks it is possible that the rumours of the Bundesbank returning to a variable repo rate will surface again," said Fernandez, who believes that these rumours would lead to price movements.

"We would see it reflected in the market and although Spain and Portugal would likely maintain the yield spread stable (except in the event of statements about EMU), it would have an effect in absolute terms, particularly in the longer yields. Over the last few days we have seen a levelling out of the curve and in a context of bund correction we might see longer yields spiking. In such a case Portugal would suffer more", he added.
However, for Lumholdt the likelihood of a return to a variable rate repo en Germany was already factored in and would not affect market prices.

"Speculations about the Bundesbank might re-surface if the current dollar trend is maintained, but in my opinion the only thing that might happen is a return to a variable repo rate and that should not have any major repercussion even if it does mean a change in the central bank's policy", he indicated.
Dealers agreed that the spread with Germany in both Spain and Portugal would remain steady around current levels.

"I don't think we will see great variations in the spread in either Spain or Portugal as there as no changes in EMU expectations", said a dealer. "It is difficult to see a change in this unless the actual process comes into question."
Lumholdt agreed, saying, "in terms of the spread with Germany I think we are trapped in a very tight range and it is difficult to see any movements outside of the current 60/65 basis points".
